nodes.name: Twice daily
nodes.notes: 07:00 and 19:00 local. Deliberately twice a day, not hourly: the source API has a monthly quota and every run costs a call whether or not it finds anything.

nodes.name: Run now (manual)
nodes.notes: For testing. Same path as the schedule, so a manual run exercises exactly what the cron will do.

nodes.name: Load profile
nodes.notes:
The search terms and the per-run cap live in the database, edited from the app — not hardcoded here. Changing what you search for should not require touching a workflow.

Note the URL has no /api prefix: that prefix belongs to Caddy, and this call goes direct over the internal Docker network.

nodes.name: Loop over searches
nodes.notes:
One title at a time (batch size 1, the default).

Two reasons: it serialises the API calls instead of firing them in parallel at a rate-limited endpoint, and it keeps each search's title paired with its own results — a fan-in would merge every title's jobs into one undifferentiated list and the fetch_log rows would lose their meaning.

nodes.name: Fetch jobs
nodes.notes:
Endpoint and parameters verified against the live API: the path is /active-jb (NOT /active-jb-7d), time_frame is REQUIRED and must be one of 1h/24h/7d/6m, and the search parameter is `title` (not `title_filter`).

neverError + fullResponse mean this node ALWAYS emits exactly one item — { statusCode, headers, body } — whatever the API does. Both parts matter: the loop only advances when something flows back into it, and an HTTP failure must stay distinguishable from an empty result. See the Wrap batch node.

This plan returns no job description — description_text is null and no parameter enables it. WF-B scores against ai_key_skills / ai_keywords / ai_requirements_summary instead.

nodes.name: Ingest
nodes.notes:
The backend does the normalising, the three-guard dedup, and the fetch_log write. This node just hands over the batch.

It returns 200 with {returned, inserted, skipped} even when everything was a duplicate — that is a normal run, not a failure, so do NOT add a retry on a low inserted count.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow: 'WF-A', message: ($json.error?.message || $json.message || 'ingest step failed'), context: { execution_id: $execution.id, node: $json.error?.name || null, detail: $json } }) }}

nodes.name: Record failure
nodes.notes:
Application-health logging, distinct from Beszel's system-health monitoring. A failure recorded here shows up in the app's error feed and in GET /stats.

It loops back into the batch loop so one failed search does not abandon the remaining ones, and its own onError is continueRegularOutput so a logging failure can never become the thing that breaks the run.
